subject.title: Bug: QA history polling drops retryable gateway errors

question: Should maintainers prioritize a focused QA-lab fix that preserves `GatewayProtocolRequestError` metadata and retries only explicitly retryable `chat.history` failures?
rationale: The issue is concrete and likely small, but it carries the protected `maintainer` label and changes live QA failure semantics, so automated repair dispatch should not choose its retry boundary without maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded QA repair
options.body: Preserve the structured gateway error across the QA wrapper and add deadline-bounded retry coverage for retryable history-rebuild responses.

options.title: Keep terminal polling semantics
options.body: Decline the retry behavior if maintainers intend history-rebuild responses to fail QA scenarios immediately despite the server retry contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded QA repair
recommendation.body: Preserve the structured gateway error across the QA wrapper and add deadline-bounded retry coverage for retryable history-rebuild responses.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter supplied the concrete live scenario and identified the exact ownership boundaries for a narrow review.
